abstract: On a spherically symmetric and static background, we study the existence of linearly stable black hole (BH) solutions in nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) with a Horndeski vector-tensor (HVT) coupling, with and without curvature singularities at the center (<math display="inline"><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>). Incorporating the electric charge <math display="inline"><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>E</mi></msub></math> and the magnetic charge <math display="inline"><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></math>, we first show that nonsingular BHs can exist only if <math display="inline"><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. We then study the stability of purely electric BHs by analyzing the behavior of perturbations in the metric and the vector field. Nonsingular electric BHs are unstable due to a Laplacian instability in the vector perturbation near the regular center. In the absence of the HVT coupling (<math display="inline"><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>), singular BHs in power-law NED theories can be consistent with all linear stability conditions, while Born-Infeld BHs encounter strong coupling due to a vanishing propagation speed as <math display="inline"><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. In power-law NED and Born-Infeld theories with <math display="inline"><mi>β</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the electric fields for singular BHs are regular near <math display="inline"><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, while the metric functions behave as <math display="inline"><mo>∝</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Nevertheless, we show that Laplacian instabilities occur for regions inside the outer horizon <math display="inline"><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></math>, unless the HVT coupling constant <math display="inline"><mi>β</mi></math> is significantly smaller than <math display="inline"><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></math>. For <math display="inline"><mi>β</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, we also reconstruct the NED Lagrangian so that one of the metric functions takes the Reissner-Nordström form. In this case, there exists a branch where all squared propagation speeds are positive, but the ghost and strong coupling problems are present around the BH center. Thus, the dominance of the HVT coupling generally leads to BH instability in the high-curvature regime.
title: Vector Horndeski black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics
